units.text: Your next decade brings a stronger pull to step back and watch, even among the people you love most. Someone close reads the quiet as distance, and you stay nearest to those who let you go silent without asking why.

In this decade you need stretches of quiet even inside your closest ties, and you notice more than you say. A friend or partner takes that quiet as coldness, and you keep closest to the people who leave you space to watch.

A year with this guest draws you inward, and you watch the people around you more than you join them. Those close to you read the silence as a step away, and what you want underneath is time alone that leaves the bond in place.
You keep an observer's eye and need quiet even inside closeness.
This decade brings a need for quiet inside your closest ties.

From your mid-thirties your home holds a quiet corner that is yours alone, even with a partner beside you. A partner reads those hours as distance unless they know the quiet is not about them. You stay longest with someone who lets you go silent at the table.

Through your Home Chapter you kept a part of yourself apart, even inside the life you shared with a partner. That habit of watching from the edge was read at home as coolness, and it cost you some of the warmth you wanted. What you carry now is the knowledge that the right person lets you be quiet.

In your Home Chapter you need hours of your own inside a shared life, and you see more of your household than you show. A partner feels that quiet as distance, even when nothing is wrong between you. Your closeness lasts with the person who leaves the door open and lets you come back in your own time.

From your late forties your eye rests on the people after you, steady and quiet, and you need time apart even from them. The younger ones read that reserve as a lack of interest. You give them most in the hours after you have had your quiet.

Your Late Chapter gave you a watcher's view of the people after you, close enough to see them and far enough to stay quiet. Some of them took the distance for indifference, and they did not always come to you. You kept that clear eye, and you are best known by those who learned to sit with your silence.

In your Late Chapter you watch the people after you more than you steer them, and you need long quiet hours of your own. Those you train read that quiet as distance and hold back their questions. What you pass on reaches furthest with the few who are at ease with your silence.

From your late teens you keep watch from the edge of every circle, at work and among friends. Colleagues read your quiet as distance and leave you out of the easy talk. You hold on to the friends who let you go quiet and still count you in.

Through your twenties you watched your circles more closely than you joined them, and you needed time apart even from good friends. Colleagues took that for coolness, and some ties thinned. You still carry the sharp eye those years trained in you.

Your Rising Chapter brings an eye that watches before it joins, and you need quiet even among the friends you like best. Colleagues and friends read that as distance and stop asking you along. You keep the friendships that let you drift off and come back.
Your next decade holds long spells on your own, and you grow steadier for them. Invitations pass you by and the house goes quiet, and you come out of it clear about whose company you miss.

In this decade you spend long stretches alone and you stand firmer inside yourself. The cost is plain in the missed invitations and the evenings nobody calls, and you know better each season which people you want back.
That year you keep more to yourself than usual, and the calm suits you. Some invitations go unanswered and the evenings stay still, and you finish the year knowing which friends you want near.
Long seasons in your own company leave you steady and self-possessed.
This decade gives you long quiet spells and a firmer hold on yourself.

From your mid-thirties your home runs quiet, and you spend long evenings alone by choice. A partner and friends feel the gap when invitations go unanswered. You come out of each quiet stretch clearer about who you miss and why.

Your Home Chapter was a quiet one, with long spells at home that you chose and kept. Some invitations lapsed, and a partner found the house too still for long stretches. You hold on to a self-possession that does not need a crowd to feel whole.

In your Home Chapter you keep long hours to yourself and you are steady in them. Your house is quiet and friends stop sending a second invitation. What you want is quiet you have chosen, and each spell of it shows you who you miss.

From your late forties you keep long seasons of your own, and you need little from the crowd. The people after you call less when they find you so self-contained. You are clearest in these years about which of them you want close.

Your Late Chapter passed in long spells of your own company, steady and unhurried. The people after you visited less than they wanted to, and some invitations went unanswered. What you kept from those years is a calm that knows who it misses.

In your Late Chapter you spend long hours alone and you are at ease in them. The price is a quiet house and the people after you waiting to hear from you. You come back from each quiet spell with a clear sense of whom you want near.

From your late teens you spend more time alone than your friends do, and you grow sure of yourself early. Many of the parties and trips of those years go on without you. You learn early which friends you want to go back to.

Through your twenties you kept long stretches for yourself, and your working years had a self-possessed calm. You turned down or missed many of the gatherings your circle built its ties on. You took from those years a clear view of the friends you missed most.

In your Rising Chapter you spend long seasons on your own, at work and outside it, and you hold steady there. Colleagues stop inviting you after a few refusals and the evenings go quiet. You leave each quiet season surer of the people you miss.
You decide fast and all the way, with no middle ground.

From your mid-thirties your home runs on a fierce, decisive drive that settles things all at once. A partner stops arguing with you, and the middle ground between you goes missing. People at home hand you the hard calls, and you carry them.

Your Home Chapter ran on an all-or-nothing resolve, and your choices at home were made fast and made whole. A partner learned to stop arguing, and much of the give and take went quiet. You still have the nerve to make a hard call when others hold back.

In your Home Chapter you decide for the household quickly and completely, with no half measures. A partner gives up the argument before it starts, and that silence costs you their view. What you want is to decide and be right, and the people at home rely on you for the hardest choices.
Your next decade carries an empty seat, and the things you strain for arrive late or thin. The same emptiness lightens any hard guest it touches, and you do best on what you already hold.
In this decade an empty seat trails your efforts, and a good part of what you reach for comes slowly or comes small. Waiting on it wears you down, and you stand firmest on work already finished.
A year with this guest holds an empty seat, and what you chase arrives later or lighter than you planned. The hard parts of that year thin out the same way, and you hold best to what is already done.
An empty seat where effort lands late or light.
This decade brings an empty seat that thins both gains and hardships.

From your late forties an empty seat stands near what you hope to hand on, and the reward of it comes slowly. The people after you take up less of your work than you planned, and waiting on them goes nowhere. You pass on most through the things you have already made.

Your Late Chapter held an empty seat, and most of what you hoped to pass on arrived later and lighter than you wanted. The same emptiness softened the hard turns of those years too. What you made with your own hands stayed with you, and the people after you still use it.

In your Late Chapter an empty seat waits close to your plans for the people after you, and what you push to give them lands lightly. Hard weights land lighter too in these years. You give the most through what you already have to hand.

From your late teens an empty seat follows your early work, and the praise or progress you chase arrives late or thin. Hard knocks in those years land thin as well. You make your best ground in your twenties on work you have already finished.

Through your twenties an empty seat stood beside your study and first jobs, and the results you pushed for landed late. The hard knocks of those years came light as well. You carry out of it a habit of building from what you already had.

Your Early Chapter had an empty seat in it, and what you reached for in your first home or at school came late or came small. Hard days at home passed lightly for the same reason. What you took from those years is a feel for what is solid in your hands.

In your Early Chapter an empty place sits beside your efforts, and what you try for at school or in your first home comes later than you want. Hard days at school weigh less as well. You stand surest on the things you already know and can do.
Your Empty Seat holds this guest, and its gift comes late or light.
On your Empty Seat this guest's cost lands late or light.
